not_found_examples.note: The ONE exception found to the 'ok:true, data.<key>:null' not-found pattern: changes_compare throws a bare, unstructured string error (no JSON envelope, no code field, no issues array) when a revision id is unknown.

missing_required_arg_examples.error_text: validation_error: input did not match the tool schema.
missing_required_arg_examples.note: Caught client-side (by the MCP tool-calling harness against the tool's JSON Schema) before any request reaches the CMS_Agent server. The error is a bare string 'validation_error: input did not match the tool schema.' — there is NO structured envelope with a code, a field name, or an issues[] array of the kind the WP-00 brief anticipated. This exact same generic string is returned for every schema violation observed in this session: a missing required property (workspace_get_node with no id, workflow_get_run_context with no projectId), and an extra/unknown property forbidden by additionalProperties:false (workspace_get_nodes called with a workflowId arg).
projectId omitted (required) -> same generic validation_error string as above.

workspace_get_nodes' schema is {additionalProperties:false, properties:{}} — it accepts NO arguments at all. Passing workflowId (even though workspace_get_graph accepts it) is rejected with the same generic validation_error string. This directly answers the WP-00 question: workspace_get_nodes does NOT accept workflowId; only workspace_get_graph does.

proxy_layer_errors_not_true_MCP_errors.description: Several verbs consistently fail with a transport-level error from the Anthropic proxy in front of the MCP session, distinct from both of the above categories: 'Error POSTing to endpoint: event: message\ndata: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":<n>,"error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Anthropic Proxy: Invalid content from server","data":null}}'. This is JSON-RPC code -32600 (Invalid Request) raised by the proxy about the SERVER's response content, i.e. the CMS_Agent MCP server sent back something the proxy could not accept as valid MCP content (most likely a literal JSON `null` at the top level, or a non-object/non-string content block) rather than a well-formed tool result or a well-formed JSON-RPC error. This was 100% reproducible (5+ consecutive attempts each) for two call shapes:

affected_calls.args_that_fail: any call where `nodeId` is present (with or without runId/executionId)
affected_calls.args_that_succeed: runId alone (no nodeId) -> returns {executions:[<full run record>]}
nodeId + runId together -> also failed once in this session (see below) but a retry combining nodeId+runId still failed consistently; only never actually returned data for this verb in this session

affected_calls.args_that_fail: no args, and projectId:'dr-lurie' — both failed identically and repeatedly

affected_calls.args_that_succeed: not tested further after workflow_get_run_cost's plan.nodeTimingAggregates was found to cover the same timing-history need
